items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Now when I was playing with Ridley, when David Jones would take a solo, the bands would take down.

ctx.x: What? Yeah, that's right. Did they ever have bands like that when you remember? I might have been. I don't know. I just wondered if they had any guys that played clarinet and trombone together, you know, would really be featured like that.

Be featured like? Like solos, trombone and clarinet? Well a duet really, the two of the together. Oh no, hardly. Hardly, huh? Hardly. Because you know they didn't know that much about music to play on. Cards you know. They just played on. Well I don't mean cards. I mean tailgate. Yeah. But I know like Yank and them used to play. But most of the time when Buddy would take a solo in our band, they would take down, you see. Now when I was playing with Ridley, when David Jones would take a solo, the bands would take…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Shots was with him a lot. Handy. Sills. David Jones.

ctx.x: What about this bass with Ridgely when you were with it? Bass with Ridgely? Mm-hmm. Did he have one when you were with it?

Yeah, I'm not sure. Shots was with him a lot. Handy. Sills. David Jones. Mm-hmm. We played out the Suburban Garden. I was playing bass. Played out the Suburban Garden in 1928. Something else I wanted to ask you about.
Did they have many bands that had singers? Oh, no. Uh-huh. They wouldn't hire singers if they were out?
